# TDPdf v1.23.7.0

**Fixes Insert Text Box discarding the editor a frame after it appears.**

Four previous releases treated this as a focus problem. Production traces show it never was one. The editor was being created, attached to the page and given keyboard focus correctly every single time — and then discarded 15 to 140 milliseconds later, before any key could be pressed and without ever losing focus. What the user saw was a text box that flickered or simply never appeared.

The cause is a layout-driven caller reaching the shared "settle any in-progress edit" step one frame after placement. When the view is set to fit the width or the page, TDPdf re-fits on a deferred callback whenever anything changes the size of the viewport — including adding the text box itself. Every one of those automatic re-fits committed and destroyed the live editor. Automatic re-fits now leave it alone; a zoom you perform yourself still settles the edit as before.

As a second layer, a text box that is brand new, still empty and never typed into is now protected from being closed by an incidental commit, whatever triggers it. Re-editing existing text is unaffected: emptying that box still means "delete this annotation".

## Diagnosing this in future

`Annotation.TextEditorClosed` now records which method requested the commit, and a new `Annotation.TextEditorCommitDeferred` event records the ones the grace period refused. Both carry a method name only — no document content, no user text. Identifying the responsible caller previously meant guessing among twenty-one of them.

## For administrators

The Intune detection rule now requires 1.23.7.0, so managed machines pick this up on the next evaluation. Assignments are unaffected.

## Verifying this download

The executable is signed by *The Doodle Project Code Signing*, a private certificate. On managed machines that trust it, the signature validates. On a machine that does not, Windows will still warn on first run. Use `SHA256SUMS.txt` to confirm the download independently.
